title: Cable selection (2)
summary: Covers the BS 7671 correction factors and completes the shower-circuit example, finding the cable rating, selecting a 16mm² cable and checking voltage drop.

sections.heading: Cable size and current rating recap
paragraphs: Cable size depends on current rating under defined installation conditions, the maximum permitted voltage drop (BS 7671 Section 525, Appendix 4 section 6.4) and earth fault loop impedance requirements (Tables 41.2, 41.3 and 41.4).

The design current Ib, type of cable, installed conditions, surrounding temperature and the type and size of protection all influence the current rating. To comply with BS 7671, Ib ≤ In ≤ Iz and It ≥ Iz.
bullets: Ib = design current of the circuit
In = rated current or current setting of the protective device
Iz = current carrying capacity of a cable for continuous service under the installation conditions
It = tabulated current carrying capacity of a cable

sections.heading: Correction factors
paragraphs: Correction factors take account of the various installation conditions.
bullets: Ca: ambient or surrounding temperature, Tables 4B1 and 4B2 of Appendix 4
Cc: circuits buried directly in the ground or in a duct in the ground, Cc = 0.9; for cables above ground Cc = 1
Cd: depth of burial, Table 4B4 of Appendix 4
Cf: if the protective device is a semi-enclosed fuse to BS 3036, Cf = 0.725, otherwise Cf = 1
Cg: grouping, Tables 4C1 to 4C6 of Appendix 4

sections.heading: Thermal insulation and soil factors
paragraphs: Ci is used when cables are enclosed in thermal insulation. BS 7671 Regulation 523.9 gives three possible values. Cs covers the thermal resistivity of soil.
bullets: Cable in a thermally insulated wall or above a thermally insulated ceiling, in contact with a thermally conductive surface on one side: current carrying capacities are tabulated in Appendix 4
Cable totally surrounded over a length greater than 0.5 m: a factor of 0.5 must be applied
Cable totally surrounded over a short length less than 0.5 m: use the factor in Table 52.2 of BS 7671
Cs: thermal resistivity of soil, Table 4B3 of Appendix 4

sections.heading: Applying the factors to the shower example
paragraphs: For the semi-enclosed fuse example, each factor is worked out in turn and then used to find the cable rating Iz.
bullets: Ca: 35°C gives 0.94 from Table 4B1 of Appendix 4
Cc = 1, as the cable is above ground
Cd does not apply, as the cable is above ground
Cf = 0.725, as protection is a semi-enclosed fuse
Cg = 0.8 from Table 4C1, as the cable is grouped with one similar cable
Ci: insulation is in contact with one side of the cable, so capacities are tabulated in Appendix 4
Cs does not apply, as the cable is above ground
Installation method: Table 4A2 Reference Method 100
From Column 2 of Table 4D5, a 16mm² cable with a rating (It) of 57 amperes is required

sections.heading: Voltage drop check
paragraphs: The final step is to test for voltage drop. The maximum permissible drop is 5% of the nominal supply voltage. The calculated drop is far below this, so the 16mm² cable is the chosen cable when semi-enclosed fuse protection is used.
bullets: Maximum volt drop = 5 × 230 ÷ 100 = 11.5 V
Table 4D5 Column 8: volt drop for 16mm² cable is 2.8 mV per ampere per metre
1.42 V is less than 11.5 V, so 16mm² meets both current carrying capacity and voltage drop requirements

quiz.q: In the shower example the protection is a semi-enclosed fuse to BS 3036. What value of Cf is applied?
quiz.why: Where the protective device is a semi-enclosed fuse to BS 3036, Cf = 0.725.

quiz.q: What is the cable rating Iz for the example with In = 30 A and factors 0.94, 1, 0.725 and 0.8?
Which cable size was chosen for the shower circuit with semi-enclosed fuse protection?
quiz.why: A 16mm² cable with a rating of 57 A is required to carry 55 A.

quiz.q: What is the maximum permissible volt drop for a 230 V supply?
Which correction factor applies to a circuit buried directly in the ground?
quiz.why: For circuits buried directly in the ground or in a duct in the ground, Cc = 0.9.

quiz.q: What factor must be applied when a cable is totally surrounded by thermal insulation over a length greater than 0.5 m?
quiz.why: Where the cable is totally surrounded over a length greater than 0.5 m, a factor of 0.5 must be applied.

quiz.q: Why does the depth of burial factor Cd not apply in the shower example?
options: The cable is installed above ground
quiz.why: As the cable is installed above ground, this factor does not apply.

quiz.q: Which factor accounts for the cable being grouped with one similar cable in the example?
quiz.why: The cable is grouped with one similar cable, giving a factor of 0.8 from Table 4C1.

Which factor is given for an ambient temperature of 35°C in the example?
